triples.relationship: questioning the sufficiency of animal offerings
triples.rationale: Micah asks whether burnt offerings and calves can be the means of taking hold of the Lord. The psalm likewise discusses continual burnt offerings, refuses calves and questions whether God eats bulls' flesh, directing attention beyond merely supplying sacrificial animals.
triples.source_text: With what shall I take hold of the Lord and grasp my God Most High? Shall I take hold of Him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?

target_units.text: I will not rebuke you concerning your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are continually before Me.
I will not receive calves from your house or young goats from your flocks.
For all the forest’s wild animals are Mine, beasts on the mountains and cattle.
I know all the birds of heaven, and the field’s beauty is with Me.
If I become hungry, I will certainly not tell you, for the inhabited world and its fullness are Mine.
Will I eat bulls’ flesh or drink goats’ blood?
